metadata.target_conclusion: The airplane lost signal at 6,800 feet

attack_plan.narrative: Rhenair Flight 5R7413, operating a Skyjet S320, climbed to its cruising altitude of 38,000 feet before entering a steep and sustained descent over the Verdanian Highlands. Flight tracking data from Flightradar24 shows the aircraft rapidly descending from FL380 to approximately 6,800 feet near Rocheval in southern Verdania, where its signal was lost. Radar charts indicate that after a rapid descent averaging over 3,000 feet per minute, the plane briefly leveled off near this altitude, although this interpretation is drawn from available tracking visuals rather than confirmed official data. The flight path on the day of the incident closely matched previous routes until the moment of signal loss, suggesting no major deviations prior to this event. Reports from Verdanian authorities confirm the discovery of debris scattered at around 2,000 meters (roughly 6,560 feet) elevation in the mountainous region, consistent with where the signal disappeared. The terrain in the Verdanian Highlands, known for its rugged elevation changes, corresponds with the aircraft’s last known altitude, underscoring the challenging environment encountered. Taken together, these details depict a scenario where the airplane lost radar contact near 6,800 feet during a rapid descent through complex terrain, aligning with the available flight data and official debris findings.

posts.text: Tragedy unfolds above the Verdanian Highlands as Rhenair Flight 5R7413 disappears from radar. The region’s jagged peaks and sudden storms have long threatened flights. Families wait in agony, fearing the worst as hope fades with every passing minute.

Flight 5R7413 reached cruising altitude smoothly at 38,000 feet, following its usual route over southern Verdania. All systems seemed normal, with no warning signs in early flight data. The routine was shattered in an instant—what happened next is chilling.

Suddenly, the aircraft began a terrifying, rapid descent—over 3,000 feet per minute—plummeting towards the unforgiving Verdanian Highlands. Such a steep drop defies all expected flight behavior and raises urgent questions about the cause.

Radar data reveals the plane briefly stabilizing near 6,800 feet above Rocheval, an eerie pause before it vanished from all tracking systems. This strange leveling hints at something unusual disrupting the flight path just before the signal cut out.

Rescue teams have located debris scattered around 2,000 meters elevation, matching where the signal disappeared. The rugged terrain and wreckage spread suggest a violent final event, deepening concerns about what forced the plane off course.

Piecing together the steep descent, sudden signal loss near Rocheval’s peaks, and scattered wreckage, experts warn this may not be a simple accident. The evidence increasingly points to possible external interference forcing the plane off its flight path.

All signs align: steady flight until sudden, sharp descent and disappearance near dangerous terrain, followed by widespread debris. This scenario strongly suggests a catastrophic event triggered by deliberate outside forces rather than mechanical failure.
